name: Biscayne National Park
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Biscayne National Park in southeastern Florida protects 172,971 acres of marine and coastal environments, making it one of the largest marine parks in the National Park System. Ninety-five percent of the park is water, encompassing Biscayne Bay, the northernmost Florida Keys, and a portion of the third-largest barrier reef in the world. Originally established as Biscayne National Monument in 1968 after a citizen-led campaign blocked a proposed industrial seaport, it was redesignated as a national park in 1980. The park preserves mangrove shorelines, the shallow waters of Biscayne Bay, the undeveloped upper Florida Keys, and living coral reefs supporting over 600 species of fish.
